element: OpenART (abstract) — Muttakin, Mondal & Roy, ICSE 2026 JAWS workshop
files: https://conf.researchr.org/details/icse-2026/jaws-2026-papers/10/OpenART-Manuscript-Driven-Support-for-Promoting-Executability-of-Software-Engineerin (abstract only; no PDF, arXiv, author page, or GitHub version found via web search)
source_note: Only the researchr.org abstract exists. Web searches (title, authors, 'OpenART' + replication package) returned only the authors' separate ICSE 2026 paper 'The State of Open Science in SE Research: A Case Study of ICSE Artifacts' (arXiv:2601.02066), which motivates OpenART but is not it. All ratings are abstract-only.

UC1.evidence: "generate structured artifact documentation, including required components, dependencies, and execution steps" (abstract)
UC1.note: Produces artifact documentation from P alone, not a venue-format appendix from P + A; partial is right.

UC2.note: No mention of translating between venue standards; absence in an abstract is weak evidence.

UC3.evidence: "extracts explicit and implicit execution-relevant information from papers to generate structured artifact documentation" (abstract)
UC3.note: Maps paper-described components to an expected layout, but no claim/result-to-file links are stated; 0 defensible, 1 arguable.

UC4.evidence: "automated identification of missing or inconsistent components in existing packages" (abstract)
UC4.note: Deliverable is a missing-components report, but the reference is the manuscript-derived layout, not a venue standard S; 2 is generous, 1 arguable.

UC5.evidence: "automated identification of missing or inconsistent components in existing packages" (abstract)
UC5.note: Current 0; rubric says detecting paper-artifact inconsistencies counts as at least partial, and 'inconsistent' here is relative to the manuscript-derived spec. Paper-side gaps are not reported.

UC6.evidence: "derives an expected artifact layout that enables (i) guided preparation of replication packages from scratch" (abstract)
UC6.note: Generates docs and layout from P (two of the four UC6 items) but no code or environment; 1 correct, 2 arguable.

B1.evidence: "mixed-method user study with SE researchers across two realistic workflows: artifact creation and artifact completion" (abstract)
B1.note: Author-facing; abstract also cites 'reviewer-friendly artifact evaluation' as a downstream aim, so 2 is arguable.

B2.evidence: "Leveraging both foundation and fine-tuned large language models, OpenART extracts explicit and implicit execution-relevant information from papers" (abstract)
B2.note: No execution stated; package completion implies inspecting file contents, so 2 arguable.

B3.evidence: "automatically deriving actionable artifact specifications directly from companion manuscripts" (abstract; title says 'Manuscript-Driven')
B3.note: Completion workflow also takes an existing package as secondary input.

B4.evidence: "Despite substantial progress in artifact availability and badging" (abstract, background only)
B4.note: Current 2; the spec is derived from each manuscript, and no venue standard or published criteria drives the tool, so 1 fits better.

B5.evidence: "generate structured artifact documentation ... From this documentation, OpenART further derives an expected artifact layout" (abstract)
B5.note: Outputs are structured docs, a layout spec, and a missing-components list; no score or badge.

disagreements: UC5: current 0, should be 1 because the abstract states it identifies 'missing or inconsistent components in existing packages' relative to the manuscript-derived spec, and the rubric counts paper-artifact inconsistency detection as at least partial (low confidence, abstract only).
B4: current 2, should be 1 because the reference spec is derived from each manuscript, not from any venue standard or published criteria; 'badging' appears only as motivation (low confidence).
UC4: current 2 is debatable (1 arguable) because the missing-components check is against the paper-derived layout, not a venue standard S.
one_line_summary: LLM framework that extracts execution-relevant info from a manuscript to generate artifact documentation and an expected layout, guiding package creation and flagging missing/inconsistent components.
